arxiv-1407-3735.title: Isovector axial vector and pseudoscalar transition form factors of Δ \Delta in QCD
arxiv-1407-3735.creator: A. Kucukarslan, U. Ozdem, A. Ozpineci
arxiv-1407-3735.description: Abstract We investigate the isovector axial vector and pseudoscalar form factors of Δ \Delta baryon by employing light-cone QCD sum rules. Numerical calculations show that the form factors can be well fitted by the exponential form. We make a comparison with the predictions of lattice QCD, chiral perturbation theory and quark model.

arxiv-2201-07677.title: Tiny, Always-on and Fragile: Bias Propagation through Design Choices in On-device Machine Learning Workflows CCS: Software and its engineering Software creation and management CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning CCS: Hardware Analysis and design of emerging devices and systems CCS: General
arxiv-2201-07677.creator: Wiebke (Toussaint) Hutiri, Aaron Yi Ding, Fahim Kawsar, Akhil Mathur
arxiv-2201-07677.description: Abstract . Billions of distributed, heterogeneous and resource constrained IoT devices deploy on-device machine learning (ML) for private, fast and offline inference on personal data. On-device ML is highly context dependent, and sensitive to user, usage, hardware and environment attributes. This sensitivity and the propensity towards bias in ML makes it important to study bias in on-device settings.

arxiv-2203-07060.title: MotionSC: Data Set and Network for Real-Time Semantic Mapping in Dynamic Environments
arxiv-2203-07060.creator: Joey Wilson, Jingyu Song, Yuewei Fu, Arthur Zhang, Andrew Capodieci, Paramsothy Jayakumar, Kira Barton, Maani Ghaffari
arxiv-2203-07060.description: Abstract This work addresses a gap in semantic scene completion (SSC) data by creating a novel outdoor data set with accurate and complete dynamic scenes. Our data set is formed from randomly sampled views of the world at each time step, which supervises generalizability to complete scenes without occlusions or traces.

arxiv-2204-08268.title: On the transcendence of a series related to Sturmian words
arxiv-2204-08268.creator: Florian Luca, Joël Ouaknine, James Worrell
arxiv-2204-08268.description: Abstract Let b b be an algebraic number with | b | > 1 |b|>1 and ℋ \mathcal{H} a finite set of algebraic numbers. We study the transcendence of numbers of the form ∑ n = 0 ∞ a n b n \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{a_{n}}{b^{n}} where a n ∈ ℋ a_{n}\in\mathcal{H} for all n ∈ ℕ n\in\mathbb{N} .

arxiv-2209-07552.title: msRep : A Fast yet Light Sparse Matrix Framework for Multi-GPU Systems DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456
arxiv-2209-07552.creator: Jieyang Chen, Chenhao Xie, Jesun S Firoz, Jiajia Li, Shuaiwen Leon Song, Kevin Barker, Mark Raugas, Ang Li
arxiv-2209-07552.description: Abstract . Sparse linear algebra kernels play a critical role in numerous applications, covering from exascale scientific simulation to large-scale data analytics. Offloading linear algebra kernels on one GPU will no longer be viable in these applications, simply because the rapidly growing data volume may exceed the memory capacity and computing power of a single GPU.

arxiv-2212-02278.title: Tracing the emergence of collectivity phenomena in small systems Thanks: Presented at Quark Matter 2022 XXIXth International Conference on Ultra-relativistic Nucleus-Nucleus Collisions
arxiv-2212-02278.creator: B. Schenke S. Schlichting P. Singh
arxiv-2212-02278.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by B. Schenke S. Schlichting P. Singh. We study initial state momentum correlations and event-by-event geometry in p+Pb collisions at s = 5.02 ​ TeV \sqrt{s}=5.02~\rm TeV by following the approach of extending the IP-Glasma model to 3D using JIMWLK rapidity evolution. On examining the non-trivial rapidity dependence of the observables, we find that the geometry is correlated over large rapidity intervals, while the initial state momentum correlations have a relatively short range in rapidity.

arxiv-2409-15153.description: Abstract . A base for a permutation group G G acting on a set Ω \Omega is a sequence ℬ \mathcal{B} of points of Ω \Omega such that the pointwise stabiliser G ℬ G_{\mathcal{B}} is trivial. The base size of G G is the size of a smallest base for G G .

arxiv-2501-16719.title: Safety-Critical Control for Aerial Physical Interaction in Uncertain Environment
arxiv-2501-16719.creator: Jeonghyun Byun, Yeonjoon Kim, Dongjae Lee, H. Jin Kim
arxiv-2501-16719.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jeonghyun Byun, Yeonjoon Kim, Dongjae Lee, H. Jin Kim. Aerial manipulation for safe physical interaction with their environments is gaining significant momentum in robotics research. In this paper, we present a disturbance-observer-based safety-critical control for a fully actuated aerial manipulator interacting with both static and dynamic structures. Our approach centers on a safety filter that dynamically adjusts the desired trajectory of the vehicle’s pose, accounting for the aerial manipulator’s dynamics, the disturbance observer’s structure, and motor thrust limits.

arxiv-2506-15146.title: TACT: Humanoid Whole-body Contact Manipulation through Deep Imitation Learning with Tactile Modality
arxiv-2506-15146.creator: Masaki Murooka, Takahiro Hoshi, Kensuke Fukumitsu, Shimpei Masuda, Marwan Hamze, Tomoya Sasaki, Mitsuharu Morisawa, Eiichi Yoshida
arxiv-2506-15146.description: Abstract Manipulation with whole-body contact by humanoid robots offers distinct advantages, including enhanced stability and reduced load. On the other hand, we need to address challenges such as the increased computational cost of motion generation and the difficulty of measuring broad-area contact.

pmc-10737258.title: A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL OF SELF-HELP GUIDED BY LAY PROVIDERS FOR GENERALIZED ANXIETY DISORDER IN OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10737258.creator: Philippe Landreville, Sébastien Grenier, Patrick Gosselin, Pierre-Hugues Carmichael
pmc-10737258.description: Low use of professional help for anxiety disorders in older adults may be due in part to limited access to mental health services. Self-help guided by lay providers (LPs) could help improve access to treatment. This study evaluated the efficacy and long-term outcomes of self-help guided by LPs for generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) in older adults.

pmc-11709485.creator: Emily Greenfest‐Allen, Otto Valladares, Prabhakaran Gangadharan, Heather White, Amanda B Kuzma, Pavel P Kuksa, Wan‐Ping Lee, Yuk Yee Leung, Li‐San Wang
pmc-11709485.description: BackgroundNIAGADS is a national data repository that offers qualified investigators access to genomic data for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related dementia. In addition, NIAGADS has made substantial effort to curate, harmonize, standardize, and disseminate AD‐relevant variant, gene, and sequence annotations from publications, functional genomics datasets, and summary statistics deposited at NIAGADS.

pmc-12766593.title: Bridging the gap in cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging artificial intelligence implementations: From ambitious goals to real-world progress using foundation models
pmc-12766593.creator: Neda Tavakoli, Amir Ali Rahsepar, Daniel Kim
pmc-12766593.description: wever, integration of deep learning into cardiac imaging workflows remains fragmented. Clinicians and researchers currently rely on separate models for ventricular segmentation, tissue characterization, functional assessment, and disease detection, each of which requires costly expert annotations and task-specific development. Recently introduced advanced deep learning foundation models offer a potential solution.

pmc-13111488.title: Cost-effectiveness of interceptive orthodontics: a long-term evaluation of early treatment strategies
pmc-13111488.creator: Sara Björns, Klara Leffler, Thomas Davidson, Anna Westerlund
pmc-13111488.description: ObjectivesMalocclusions occur at high frequencies in children and adolescents. While early orthodontic (interceptive) interventions may reduce the need for later comprehensive treatment, their cost-effectiveness in publicly funded health systems is unclear. This study compares the cost-effectiveness of interceptive orthodontic care and fixed-appliance therapy, focusing on total costs, treatment outcomes, and resource use.

pmc-13145672.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1515 ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE IN THE SETTING OF INFECTIVE ENDOCARDITIS: A RETROSPECTIVE CLINICAL OVERVIEW
pmc-13145672.creator: Elena-Grațiela Vodă, Alexandra Ciresa, Ioana Georgescu, Veronica Indries, Cristina Plesa, Carmen Sirbu
pmc-13145672.description: Background and aimsInfective endocarditis (IE) is an uncommon but important cause of cardioembolic acute ischemic stroke (AIS), associated with diagnostic uncertainty and complex therapeutic decision-making. Stroke occurring in the setting of IE represents a distinct clinical entity with heterogeneous presentation and outcomes. We aimed to provide a descriptive clinical and microbiological overview of AIS associated with infective endocarditis.

pmc-13206544.title: Climate and seed mass drive intraspecific variation in seed longevity in storage
pmc-13206544.creator: Lea Klepka, Sascha Liepelt, Anna Bucharova
pmc-13206544.description: PremiseConservation seed banks are essential for ex situ plant conservation, but stored seeds slowly deteriorate and lose viability. Seed longevity in storage is determined by the initial seed viability and the rate of seed viability loss. The rate of seed viability loss in storage varies between species and possibly between populations or even genotypes within species.

pmc-13435342.title: Early Serum Free Light Chain Response in Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma: Documented Earlier Than MRD and Complementary in Prognosis
pmc-13435342.creator: Yubiao Pan, Yue Wang, Yaqin Xiong, Panpan Li, Chenqi Yu, Peng Liu
pmc-13435342.description: Minimal residual disease (MRD) is the standard for deep response assessment in multiple myeloma but requires bone marrow sampling. Whether early serum free light chain (sFLC) response provides independent prognostic information in real‐world, predominantly non‐transplant patients remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed 701 patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated at a single Chinese center (2015–2021).

pmc-13538993.title: Bone turnover biomarkers and semi-quantitative bone histomorphometry in chronic kidney disease: Comparison between patients with and without fractures
pmc-13538993.creator: Sushil Sharma, Premjit Sujir, Pranav Rajasekharan, Prem Kotian, Manikanta Bhupal, G. N. Sudhanva, Karthik Parimi
pmc-13538993.description: BackgroundChronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with increased fracture risk not fully explained by reduced bone mineral density. CKD–mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD), involving abnormalities in bone turnover, mineralization, and microarchitecture, contributes to skeletal fragility. However, the relationship between routine biochemical markers and semi-quantitative bone histomorphometry remains inadequately defined, particularly in resource-limited settings and the Indian population.

pmc-13682579.title: Socioeconomic status and loss to follow-up after orthopedic trauma surgery
pmc-13682579.creator: Yvonne Tan, Mina Tohidi, Imran Syed, Jeff Yach
pmc-13682579.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:Follow-up after surgery is important, to monitor patient recovery and to identify potential complications. Our primary objective was to determine the association between patient socioeconomic status and loss to follow-up after orthopedic trauma surgery.Methods:We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients aged 18 to 75 years who underwent orthopedic trauma surgery at a trauma centre in Ontario between January 2022 and December 2023. Patient socioeconomic status was determined by linking postal code with Material and Social Deprivation Index and presented as quintiles.
